Nernst-Einstein Ionic Conductivity Relation:
σ_ion = (n · q² · D_Li) / (k_B · T)

Comparison of Solid Electrolyte Families:
- Sulfides (LGPS, Argyrodites): σ_ion ≈ 10 to 25 mS/cm (exceeds liquid electrolyte speed), highly ductile, but releases toxic H₂S gas upon ambient moisture exposure.
- Oxides (Garnet LLZO, NASICON): σ_ion ≈ 1 mS/cm, chemically stable against high-voltage cathodes, but extremely brittle with high interfacial contact resistance.
- Halides (Li₃InCl₆): σ_ion ≈ 1 to 5 mS/cm, highly oxidative stability (> 4.5 V), excellent compatibility with high-nickel cathodes.

items: Critical Current Density (CCD): The maximum charging current rate beyond which non-uniform lithium plating initiates intergranular short circuits.

items: Stack Compression Engineering: Design cell housings with spring-loaded mechanical platens to maintain continuous interfacial contact through 20% state-of-charge thickness swings.
Dry Room Manufacturing: Sulfide solid electrolyte production requires ultra-dry atmospheres (dew point < -50°C) to prevent lethal hydrogen sulfide decomposition.
High-Nickel Cathode Coupling: Pair solid electrolytes with single-crystal NMC90 cathodes coated in lithium borate to eliminate micro-cracking at high cell voltages (> 4.3V).
